priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the frozen Claude v15 REJECT (7b8c6e49), and an error of mine is directly in scope. At v15 I recorded HAE14-CX-01 as fully repaired and quoted FC-ROUND-TRIP's clause as evidence the projection was protected. That clause read 'must still carry generation and manifest digest, or policyProvenance (...)'. The disjunction meant a denied CA-1 record could satisfy it by carrying policyProvenance instead of generation and manifest digest, weakening a v14 obligation rather than adding to it. Codex caught that as HAE15-CX-01. I quoted the sentence and did not parse it. That is my third under-call in this lineage after the D-032 attribution at v9 and the advisory omission at v14, and the first that is substantive rather than bookkeeping. The correction I carried into this round was to state, for each claimed repair, what the clause permits rather than only what it requires, and to check disjunctions and scope words explicitly. I also front-loaded the check my own v15 finding predicts would fail, that a per-round completeness repair lands for the round complained about and lags for the round doing the complaining. It did not fail. Recording an ACCEPT after five consecutive REJECTs from me carries its own risk of fatigue or of rewarding a successor that answered my findings, so the verdict below rests on mechanical checks I can reproduce rather than on the impression that the artifact has improved.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is ACCEPT. All three claimed repairs are complete and each was verified mechanically rather than read: the FC-ROUND-TRIP disjunction I personally misread at v15 is gone, with the denied-CA-1 obligation restored as its own unconditional sentence; my CLAUDE-HEA15-S1 is discharged with the four v14 advisories registered, the overclaiming disposition amended, and the governing rule's own or tightened to and; and Codex's HAE15-CX-02 produced a GOVERNING registerCoverageRule whose check I executed myself across fourteen frozen verdict files for zero discrepancies in either direction. Custody is clean on every pin, all 49 recorded inputs reproduce, the D-032 section reproduces, and no prior-generation repair has regressed. Critically, the failure this lineage produces most reliably, a completeness repair that lags by exactly one round, was my first test and did not occur: the v15 round is itself complete. I then ran a deliberate substantive sweep outside the bookkeeping, across failClosed, coveredActs, outcomeVocabulary, effectCommit and the join blockers, and found no inconsistency. The three standing advisory subjects persist and are recorded as an advisory; their consequence has not changed and escalating them in the one round where I have no other finding would be reclassification rather than review. On the evidence I can reproduce, this candidate meets the bar.
